correctness.rationale: Exact finite theorem: all 65536 subsets of the 16-point source are tested for ideals (430 survive); maps are enumerated with complete component assignments (2836) and independently checked by recursive linear-extension generation. A full 2824-line certificate has every current-poset beat witness checked by the package script, yielding exactly four constant maps forming C and eight incomparable isolated projection/automorphism maps. A Stong beat deletion is a strong deformation retraction; the terminal 12-point core has homotopy S1 plus 8 points, hence \(H_1\cong\mathbb Z\), \(H_0\cong\mathbb Z^9\) and no higher integral homology. The certificate checker is supplied for replay from the package paths. The claim does not generalize from a finite experiment to an infinite family.

value.rationale: A finite mapping space is a natural homotopy invariant in finite topology; determining its complete homotopy type resolves a specific gap left by a published complete \(\pi_0\) census. The previously unresolved 2828-map component is shown to have nonzero integral \(H_1\), not just connectedness. The result identifies a concrete compact-open function-space strong core for a canonical minimum-size torus model and makes a useful componentwise comparison with classical \(\operatorname{Map}(T^2,S^1)\), without asserting an unsupported general theorem.
